newsitem.title: UK: Davis Service 70 mln stg loan for acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Davis Service 70 mln stg loan for acquisition.

text.p: LONDON, September 5 (LPC) - Davis Service Group Plc has borrowed 70 million stg from Midland Bank to help finance its proposed 136.5 million stg acquisition of Spring Grove Services, Davis finance director George Boyle said.
Textile maintenance company Davis Service announced Thursday that it has agreed to buy rival Spring Grove from Granada Group in an all cash deal.

The credit has a seven-year final maturity and is priced 60 bps over LIBOR, Boyle said. The loan begins to amortise in its third year with optional payments in years one and two. Midland intends to keep the entire credit in its portfolio.
Davis also proposes a one-for-three rights issue of covertible stock unit to raise 71.5 million stg.

At December 31 1996 Davis Service will have gearing of about 65 percent according to Boyle. By June 30 1997, after the acquisition is completed, interest cover should be between six and seven times, he said.
In addition to the Midland loan, Davis has outstanding bank debt of 25 million stg from Lloyds Bank and 5 million stg from Barclays Bank.
